newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan airport strike causes major cargo delays.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan airport strike causes major cargo delays.

text.p: Air cargo giant Lufthansa Cargo and freight forwarders in Nairobi on Monday called for urgent government action to find a solution to a strike at Nairobi's Jomo Kenyata airport which is causing major delays to air cargo.
Lufthansa said the majority of their Frankfurt-bound perishable cargo over the weekend had been more than 24 hours delayed because of the problems in Nairobi, which resulted in lost connections.

Both Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International Airport and the Moi International Airport in Mombasa have been crippled since midnight Friday, when air traffic controllers went on strike demanding better pay and working conditions.

Airlink, an 85 percent-owned subsidiary of Swiss freight forwarders Kuehne & Nagel, said it stood to loose an entire cargo of fresh cut flowers, which have awaited flight connection to Johannesburg since Saturday.

"We have had delays on all our flights which is very bad because the aircraft rotation time is very tight and two hours delay at this end can result in loosing our trucking connection at the other end," said David Keary, Lufthansa Cargo's general manager for East and Central Africa.
"So you could loose a whole day in distribution which is critical when you are dealing with perishable goods, which is what has happened in most cases," he added.

A Lufthansa Cargo Boeing-747 freighter scheduled for departure Saturday morning was more than two hours delayed whilst ten Airbus passenger flights, which also carry smaller loads of cargo, on both Saturday and Sunday were delayed for hours.

Airlink was scheduled to fly some five tonnes of cut flowers to Johannesburg Saturday morning, but due to the go-slow the flight was cancelled and by Monday noon the cargo load had still not left Nairobi.
"This is a major problem, all of it is perishable cargo which was going to Johannesburg for connecting flights to Taipei and Australia.

"Now it's two days delayed and if we can't make it with the connecting flights we will have to cancel the cargo. We are still trying to get it on the first possible flight, but the Kenya Airways flight scheduled for 9.30 local time (0600 GMT) Monday morning still has not departed," an official with Airlink said at 1300 local (10.00 GMT).
Airlink had another of their own freight charters scheduled for Johannesburg on Monday, but they did not know if it would make it, he added.
Airlink also had booked some 20 tonnes of cargo shipments with British Airways, Emirates, Gulf Air and Olympic Air, which had all been delayed causing some inbound cargo to be stranded.

David Keary said Lufthansa Cargo was preparing a written expression of concern to the government, urging them to take immediate action as the strike was greatly damaging to both the industry and the economy.

"It definitively jeopardises the business when you are dealing with perishable goods and if it continues much longer it can damage Kenya's reputation as being unreliable for delivery, as well as it's bad for passengers," said Keary.
"I am going to express concern to the government of the damage it does to both the industry and the economy, they (the government) should be aware of the fact that this is very damaging," he said.
